conflicts: Verification pass (2026-10-02): 12453.14 (J = 11/2): the constants 370.011, 660.165 MHz are the J = 11/2 fit of an unidentified lower level in Childs 1992 (Table 3 there; J = 9/2 fits equally well with A = 444.022, B = 519.105 MHz); only the compilation of Elantkowska et al. 2017 assigns them to 12453.14. 4018.21 (J = 1/2): Elantkowska et al. cite Childs 1970 for A = 2584.8(4.0) MHz, an uncertainty far larger than in the other Childs 1970 rows; kept as printed, original not opened.

Hyperfine constants of the low even levels measured by Childs 1970 (atomic-beam magnetic resonance) are quoted with slightly different numbers by two later sources: Elantkowska et al. 2017 (Table 3) and the 'previous values' column of Childs & Goodman 1979 (Table II). 462.08: A = 472.643(2), B = 1154.239(17) vs 472.646(1), 1154.271(11); 509.845: 577.465(2), 989.917(30) vs 577.472(1), 990.046(10); 1371.045: 602.219(3), 1267.267(30) vs 602.232(1), 1267.402(11); 2310.09: 405.106(3), -92.638(50) vs 405.118(1), -92.432(13); 2840.17: 441.771(5), 158.750(40) vs 441.792(2), 158.966(12); 4646.83: 481.738(2), 2245.914(50) vs 481.740(1), 2246.145(13) MHz. The differences exceed the stated uncertainties (probably values with and without second-order corrections; the original paper could not be opened to decide). The Elantkowska-quoted values are kept as the entry, the others are under 'alternatives'.

285.5, 462.08, 509.845: the 1966 Fabry-Perot values of Arnoult & Gerstenkorn (530.6(6.0)/989(60), 470.7(6.0)/1169(60), 572.6(6.0)/1049(60) MHz) agree with the atomic-beam values within their errors; they are kept as alternatives.

4695.505 (8D5/2): Childs 1992 laser-rf (A = 215.703, B = -401.605 MHz, first-order fit, no error printed) vs Childs 1970 as quoted by Elantkowska et al. 2017 (215.653(15), -401.862(60)). The 1992 direct value is kept.

Level 23147.92: Elantkowska et al. 2017 (Table 3) list it in the J = 13/2 block with A = 708.9(0.6), B = 1328(29) MHz (Stefanska & Furmann, private communication), while NIST gives J = 15/2 for this level. Because fitted hyperfine constants depend on the assumed J, this value was NOT entered on the level.

Malcheva et al. 2013 state in their abstract that time-resolved laser-induced-fluorescence lifetimes of Tb I are systematically shorter than the older delayed-coincidence values (numbers not accessible).
not_found: Lifetimes of every drawn excited level (19131.45, 23043.43, 23107.25, 23147.92, 25076.26, 25717.68, 25825.53, 26087.13, 26385.99, 27102.94 cm^-1): measured by Malcheva, Engstrom, Lundberg, Nilsson, Hartman, Blagoev, Phys. Scr. 88, 045304 (2013) (7 odd + 11 even levels) and Feng et al., J. Phys. B 43, 225001 (2010) (27 odd levels at 27220-33293 cm^-1, 6.5-43.9 ns). Still closed. Routes tried this pass: OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar (both 'closed', no repository copy), Lund portal record lup.lub.lu.se/record/4172110 (metadata only, no file), OSTI ETDEWEB records 22191244 and 21444083 (abstract only), arXiv API (no preprint), Wayback Machine captures of the IOP pages (abstract only; PDF captures are redirects). The 2022 paper that reprints these lifetimes (Experimental branching fractions, transition probabilities and oscillator strengths in Tb I, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer, doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2022.108354, flagged 'bronze' open) answers HTTP 403 to automated access and has no Wayback copy.
Transition probabilities / branching fractions of Tb I lines: exist in doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2022.108354 (see above), not accessible; NIST lists no A values for Tb I.

Childs, Phys. Rev. A 2, 316 (1970) itself (APS, closed; no OSTI or repository copy found): its hyperfine constants are now entered second-hand from Elantkowska et al. 2017 and Childs & Goodman 1979. The constants of 6H°13/2 (2771.675) are in neither of those tables and stay missing (Childs et al. 1984 was re-read from a Wayback copy of the abstract page: its Tables 3 and 6 give 159Tb data for 6H°11/2 only).

Hyperfine constants of the drawn odd excited levels (19131.45, 25076.26, 26087.13, 26385.99, 27102.94) and of the even 23107.25, 25717.68, 25825.53: the Poznan papers on the odd-parity system (Furmann et al., J. Phys. B 50 (2017), doi:10.1088/1361-6455/aa8370; JQSRT 2019 doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2019.106613; JQSRT 2023 doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2023.108492) and Wang et al., J. Anal. At. Spectrom. 2024 (doi:10.1039/d3ja00160a) are closed (IOP captcha, Elsevier 403, RSC). Furmann et al., J. Phys. B 49, 025001 (2016) is flagged open at IOP but the site serves a captcha page; its two levels (9145.23, 9897.73) were taken second-hand from Elantkowska et al. 2017. The full version of Table 3 of Elantkowska et al. is in a supplementary file that was not retrieved (the printed table already contains all 86 experimental A values the authors used).

Laser cooling: the feasibility study (Search for the laser-cooling schemes in the terbium atom, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 2025, doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2025.109375) is closed and has no arXiv version; no experimental cooling of Tb found.
Precise transition frequencies and measured level energies beyond NIST: none found.
notes: 159Tb is the only stable isotope (I = 3/2), so there are no isotope shifts between stable isotopes. Hyperfine constants: 94 levels now carry A (and mostly B). Sources actually opened: (1) Elantkowska et al., Eur. Phys. J. Plus 132, 455 (2017) (open access; PDF from the Wayback copy of the Springer file, saved as pdf/Tb_Elantkowska_2017.pdf) - its Table 3 compiles all measured A, B of even-parity levels with the original reference per row (Childs 1970; Childs & Goodman 1979; Childs 1992; Furmann et al. 2015, 2016; Stefanska et al. 2017; private communication); these are stored with method 'compilation'. (2) Childs & Goodman, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 69, 815 (1979) and Childs, J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 9, 191 (1992): the tables embedded in the publisher abstract pages, read from Wayback Machine copies (saved as pdf/Tb_Childs_1979.html, pdf/Tb_Childs_1992.html); values measured in those papers are 'experiment'. (3) Arnoult & Gerstenkorn 1966 and Childs et al. 1984, read on the publisher abstract pages in the first pass. Eight levels with hyperfine data from Childs & Goodman 1979 are odd-parity upper levels (17118.72, 17341.92, 17409.62, 18461.87, 19450.45, 19658.41, 21837.92, 22223.87). Sign convention: A, B in MHz as printed. Still no lifetime and no transition rate for Tb I (see not_found). Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: top-level ionization_limit; transition field use_source; hyperfine field C_MHz (magnetic-octupole fit constant, 5425.06 only).
